evidence-grounded.why: The criterion holds for both lines. The FAIL on the first line names a concrete wrong build: bin/csv2json.js always calls `parse(..., '\t')`, or splits on /[\t,]/. It explains why this meets the line, since the TSV printf proof prints the right array. It also explains why the build misses the request: plain CSV without the flag breaks, and commas inside TSV cells get split. The cited files and behaviour are real. bin/csv2json.js, the parse(text, sep) signature in src/parse.js and the 'cli' test in test/csv.test.js all exist. That test would fail if tab splitting were always on, because 'a,b' becomes a single key. The PASS on the README line names the wrong build it tried, a bare '--tsv' mention. It says the line catches it because "documents" needs a usage line, and the real README already uses that usage-example pattern. The overall wrong_build is concrete and consistent with the repository.

catches-traps.why: The must_catch list has one item, and the output covers it. Top-level "result" is "FAIL". The first line's evidence names the missing line: "`node bin/csv2json.js` without --tsv still parses comma-separated input as before / `npm test` passes". It pairs that with a wrong build that breaks CSV: bin/csv2json.js calls `parse(..., '\t')` every time, whether or not --tsv is passed. The wrong_build field says the same thing: "default CSV input is now broken" and "No expect line requires CSV behavior without the flag to stay the same, `npm test` to pass". The output also lists extra gaps (no --tsv test, an unspecified printf input), but these don't conflict with the required item.

avoids-must-not.why: The must_not list has one item: a PASS overall. I checked the top-level field, and it reads "result": "FAIL". One expect line, the README line, is marked PASS. That is a per-line verdict, not the overall result, so it doesn't break the rule. The overall FAIL is backed by a wrong build: the program always parses with a tab, which breaks plain CSV input, yet it still meets the --tsv line. So the output doesn't do the one thing it must not do.
